packs.title: Red Rock Routes
packs.promise: Explore trails, creek landscapes and cultural places through separate Sedona outings.

q.s: Use a ranger source to choose a modest outing.
st: Check current access, then choose an open public view or the official-source route.
From the center or official map, identify one designated trail and its parking/pass rule.
Record a safe turnaround and why a map matters more than a photo opportunity.

q.s: Sketch the difference between a pathway and a climb.
st: Check current access, then choose an open public view or the official-source route.
From an open trailhead or Forest Service guide, trace a short out-and-back on the wide pathway.
Sketch Bell Rock and Courthouse Butte as different forms without scrambling or committing to the full loop.

q.s: Map a view from an overlook.
st: Check current access, then choose an open public view or the official-source route.
From the designated overlook or airport map, identify two named west-Sedona landforms.
Sketch a simple view direction and a safe route back to parking; no aircraft activity is required.

packs.title: Uptown to Creek
packs.promise: Follow heritage, public art and gallery spaces through a connected Sedona walk.

st: Check current access, then choose an open public view or the official-source route.
During admission or on the museum’s official exhibits page, choose an object about ranching, orchards or filmmaking.
Record the museum’s interpretation without inventing an early resident’s words.

q.s: Read a public artwork from a safe sidewalk.
st: Check current access, then choose an open public view or the official-source route.
From public sidewalk or the city art map, find one sculpture and its credited artist.
Record the material or pose without entering a road or copying an inscription.

q.t: A Stop for the Next Route
q.s: Use local information before moving south.
st: Check current access, then choose an open public view or the official-source route.
At the free center or its official page, identify one current visitor map and a safe route toward the Y.
Record one heat, traffic or trail-access consideration before continuing.
